episodes.159851: A stalled boundary across the region, combined with an influx of moisture and humid airmass, led to afternoon showers and thunderstorms across eastern Kentucky. These storms resulted in heavy rainfall, which caused flash flooding in portions of Laurel County. Another storm resulted in strong wind gusts and downed trees in Letcher County.
episodes.159889: Widespread street flooding occurred across the City of Houston as the collision of two boundaries resulted in the development of near-stationary strong thunderstorms. Additionally, frequent lightning strikes resulted in some property damage.
episodes.159938: Thunderstorms repeatedly moved across the area on the afternoon of the 15th, producing flash flooding in Jackson County.
episodes.160042: A midlevel disturbance trekked across the region. This feature tapped into low-level moisture to produce scattered showers and thunderstorms. The stronger storms produced gusty winds in excess of 70 mph at the Cortez Municipal Airport.
episodes.160254: Plenty of tropical moisture ahead of Tropical Storm Fred along with an upper level disturbance approaching West Virginia from the west led to slow moving showers and storms on August 16th. A mudslide occurred in the town of Welch and high water occurred south of the Twin Branch community due to blocked culverts in McDowell County.
episodes.160642: Thunderstorms developed across Southwestern Montana in a warm, dry air mass ahead of an approaching cold front. These showers and thunderstorms produced widespread gusty outflow winds, including one that caused a 63 mph wind gust in Beaverhead County.
episodes.160704: Afternoon storms produce strong marine wind gusts around Tampa Bay.
episodes.160735: Thunderstorm wind gusts resulted in damage to a home in Powell. Motorists were rescued from a stalled vehicle near Cleveland.
episodes.161133: Deep tropical moisture streaming over the region from passing TS Fred fueled a few convergent bands of training convection across the local area. Storms in these bands produced locally heavy rainfall and gusty winds.
episodes.161287: A weak disturbance that moved over the Billings Forecast area resulted in the development of a few thunderstorms that produced some severe wind gusts.
episodes.161730: An upper level low was centered in central Oklahoma within a trough that extended from the Great Lakes to West Texas.  The trough combined with abundant monsoonal moisture, modest instability, and wind shear led to scattered strong to severe thunderstorms that developed in the Texas Panhandle during the afternoon hours. Some of these storms produced hail up to 1 inch in diameter and some minor nuisance flooding. However, strong to at times damaging damaging winds were the main impact from these storms which damaged trees and tops of a few buildings.
episodes.161924: A boundary remain draped overhead while a deep southerly flow ushered in plenty of moisture. Showers and thunderstorms resulted in heavy rainfall that led to instances of flooding and flash flooding.
episodes.162213: A thunderstorm moved through Lake Charles causing flooding in south sections of the city.
episodes.162302: After moving across the Greater Antilles and weakening, the remnants of Tropical Storm Fred strengthened into a tropical storm once again in the Gulf of Mexico and made landfall near Cape San Blas with maximum sustained winds near 65 mph on August 16th. The storm brought flooding and strong winds to numerous areas of the tri-state region. Rainfall amounts were generally in the 3 to 9 inch range with the highest amounts in Bay and Washington counties. Inundation along the coast generally remained below 3 ft MHHW, except for Apalachicola which measured 3.37 ft MHHW. One man was injured when a tree fell onto his car in Millville in Bay county, and one indirect fatality of a 51 year old male occurred due to hydroplaning in Bay county.
episodes.162485: Afternoon thunderstorms along the boundary between the Atlantic and Lake Okeechobee breezes helped to form a waterspout over Lake Okeechobee.
episodes.162505: A supercell thunderstorm tracked across Rice county on Sunday, August 15th producing extremely strong straight-line winds and hail up to the size of baseballs. Strong winds blew over railroad cars and snapped power poles. Winds were estimated to be near 110 mph at the peak of the storm.
episodes.162512: On the 14th, a cold front worked its way south through central Kentucky to Tennessee, but by the 16th, the slow moving front was on its way back north as a warm front. Even though the threat of severe weather was low, the moist environment produced isolated flash flooding in two central Kentucky counties.
episodes.162679: Increasing moisture and southeast upslope flow well in advance of landfalling Tropical Cyclone Fred resulted in development of numerous showers across the high elevations of the Balsams and surrounding hours during the overnight and early morning hours. Heavy rain showers moving repeatedly over the same locations resulted in locally very high rainfall amounts of as much as 12 inches in just a few hours. This resulted in the most significant flash flooding along the upper French Broad River in almost 20 years. Additional flash flooding developed in Lincoln County later in the day after a small area of excessive rainfall developed over the Piedmont.
episodes.162695: Multiple rounds of thunderstorms developed and moved across southeast Arizona from mid morning of August 16 through the early evening of August 17. Individual storms produced heavy rain of 1 to 2 inches per hour, but some locations where multiple thunderstorm events occurred received 3 to 4 inches of rain during the period. The result was numerous reports of flash flooding, road closures and swift water rescues, especially in Pima and Cochise counties. Longer term flooding occurred in the Brawley Wash and downstream in Greene Wash. Damage from thunderstorm winds and lightning also occurred in the Tucson Metro.
episodes.162713: Scattered thunderstorms along a frontal boundary produced heavy rain which caused flash flooding across portions of central Virginia.
episodes.162739: A stationary boundary continued to drape across west central Kansas that sparked a few isolated storms moving out of northwest Kansas and Nebraska. A small MCS pushed south during the evening hours with ample CAPE values but weak shear and lapse rates. Severe hail up to 1.5 inches were reported during this timeframe along the Hwy 283 corridor.
episodes.162754: Scattered thunderstorms along a frontal boundary produced heavy rain which caused flooding and flash flooding across portions of central and southeast Virginia.
episodes.162805: Thunderstorms across northern Arizona produced strong winds and hail as monsoon moisture remained over the area.
episodes.162810: Deep moisture over northern Arizona allowed severe thunderstorms to form and produce damaging wind, heavy rain, and hail.
episodes.162842: Strong high pressure centered over the Great Basin and an inverted trough near the Arizona/Mexico international border promoted enhanced east/northeast steering flow favorable for maintaining thunderstorms off the high terrain into the lower elevations. A very moist and unstable atmosphere promoted the development of strong to severe thunderstorms that pushed off the high terrain of southern Gila County and into the lower deserts during the evening of the 15th. Several instances of damage were reported, which included multiple downed trees in the Mesa area. No injuries were reported.
episodes.162907: An upper trough combined with deep monsoonal moisture over the region to bring heavy rain and flash flooding to the San Lorenzo area.

events.narrative: Highway 192, near the U.S. Post Office, had approximately 6 inches of water flowing over the road in southern London. Water receded by 9 PM EDT.
A quick 5 to 6 inches of rain produced street flooding in south Lake Charles near Barb High School. The emergency manager reported water began to enter his residence near the school.
High water was reported on Hull Street Road near Bellson Park Drive.
Spotter reported fast moving water on Pemberton Road near Interstate 64.
High water was reported at the intersection of East River Road and Dupuy Avenue.
County Road 32 in Hollywood had 4 to 6 inches of slowing water reported covering the roadway.
High water was reported along Whitehead Road.
Multiple trees were reported down on Highway 1862 in the community of Thorton.
Damaging wind gusts moving through the Roosevelt Lake area resulted in a metal carport roof being blown off. Wind gusts estimated to be between 50-60 mph. No injuries were reported.
Two people were rescued from a car stalled on a flooded roadway.

Estimated pea-sized hail fell for approximately one hour and caused significant crop damage around the property of Reevis Mountain School. Most of the fruit trees were affected, with the peach and jujube harvests deemed total losses. Nearly an acre of vegetable leaves were shredded. Many of the walnuts and all pecans fell off their trees. Damage costs were not provided.

A picture on social media showed a large pine tree down at an apartment complex near McKellips Road and Higley Road in Mesa. Wind estimated to be between 50-60 mph based on nearby observations and radar. No injuries were reported.

A large pine tree approximately 2-3 feet in diameter fell on top of a garage and a vehicle near University Drive and Greenfield Road in Mesa. No injuries were reported. Timing was estimated using radar.

Multiple large pine trees and power poles were blown down at an apartment complex along University Drive between Val Vista Drive and Lindsay Road. Additional downed trees were reported in this area. No injuries were reported. Timing was estimated using radar.
Quarter sized hail (1 inch diameter) was reported by three different sources around Chino Valley.

Photos on social media showed several large trees down along with damage to a playground in an area near Arizona Avenue between Elliot Road and Warner Road. A large tree estimated to be approximately 2-3 feet in diameter was uprooted at an apartment complex at Warner Road and Evergreen Street. No injuries were reported.
A weather station north-northeast of Iron Springs recorded a peak wind gust of 58 MPH at 11:29 PM MST from a thunderstorm. Wind gusts to 56 MPH continued for another 10 minutes.
A peak wind gust of 71 MPH was measured by the automated weather station at the Cortez Municipal Airport.

Stream gauges indicated and an NWS flood survey confirmed significant flash flooding developed near the upper reaches of the French Broad River after as much as a foot of rain fell in the headwaters in less than six hours. Multiple structures along the river were inundated in the town of Rosman, including on Depot St, Highway 178, Main St, and Chestnut St. This was the worst flooding along this portion of the French Broad in almost 30 years, while the stream gauge at Rosman registered its 4th-highest level on record. (Continuous observations at that site date back to 1935). Newspaper reported significant flash flooding also occurred upstream of Rosman along the North Fork of the French Broad in the Balsam Grove community, where vehicles were swept downstream and multiple structures were damaged or destroyed. In addition, flash flooding developed along the Davidson River in Pisgah Forest, briefly inundating portions of Davidson River Rd and Deavor Rd.
Ware Bottom Spring Road (Route 898) was closed due to standing water over the roadway.

Spotter provided video evidence of a tributary of the South Fork Catawba River overflowing its banks onto River Rd after 3 to 5 inches of rain fell over north central Lincoln County in just a few hours.
Spotter  estimates a 60 mph gust with trees bending  nearly 90 degrees.
